teams.heading: Fiji face defensive deficit after conceding 145 points in Nations Championship
teams.body: Fiji currently occupy 12th place in the Nations Championship following a winless start to the tournament's opening three rounds. While the attack has scored 49 points, the Flying Fijians have conceded 145 across their fixtures, including the recent 17-33 loss to Scotland. This leaves the side with a points difference of -96 as they prepare for the fourth round. The squad must now look to tighten their defensive structure before the upcoming meeting with France.

teams.heading: Zoe Harrison scores overtime winner as England Women defeat New Zealand
teams.body: England Women returned to winning ways as Zoe Harrison’s 81st-minute intercept try secured a 26-19 victory over New Zealand at Allianz Stadium. Following the draw with Canada that halted their 39-match winning streak, the Red Roses lacked clinical edge and trailed 12-7 at the interval. After Marlie Packer departed with concussion, Harrison redeemed an earlier penalty miss to settle the WXV Global Series clash. Head coach John Mitchell noted the value of the scrap, saying: "It’s important to learn how to win tight Test matches."

teams.heading: France sustain winning momentum across their recent five international rugby fixtures
teams.body: France approach the upcoming autumn international window with a solid run of form, having secured three victories in their last five matches. The team is currently on a two-match winning streak, most recently defeating Japan 42-15 away from home during the July Nations Championship group stage. With a record of three wins and two losses over that five-game sequence, the squad enters the next phase of their schedule building upon their latest result.

teams.heading: Ireland Women make six changes for WXV clash against Japan today
teams.body: Ireland Women look for a strong response in Galway after last week's 40-36 defeat to the USA. Head coach Scott Bemand has made six personnel changes, including a first start for Eilís Cahill in the front row and the inclusion of Neve Jones at hooker. With Aoife Wafer ruled out due to a minor training injury, the side aims to improve their attacking prowess against Japan. Bemand noted the match serves as an ideal opportunity to add layers to their game.

teams.heading: Zebre Parma suffer heavy defeat as Bulls secure bonus-point victory
teams.body: Zebre Parma began their United Rugby Championship campaign with a difficult 47-13 home defeat against a rampant Bulls side on Saturday night. Despite controlling the opening 20 minutes and leading early through a Tommaso Allan penalty, the hosts were undone by the visitors’ seven-try haul. Alessandro Fusco provided a moment of individual quality for the home supporters by stepping over in the final quarter, but the Bulls’ physicality ultimately proved too much for the Zebre defence to handle.

teams.heading: Scotland Women suffer heavy defeat after Australia overturn half-time lead
teams.body: Scotland Women fell to a 30-10 loss against Australia at Hive Stadium on Saturday, surrendering a 10-5 interval advantage. Despite an opening try from Evie Gallagher and a penalty from Helen Nelson, the hosts were overpowered by three Australian tries in an eight-minute spell after the break. The dismissal of Gallagher for a professional foul proved a turning point, allowing the Wallaroos to secure 25 unanswered points. The sides are scheduled to meet again in Sydney next weekend.

teams.heading: Cardiff defeat Scarlets in first Welsh derby of new season
teams.body: Cardiff secured victory in the opening Welsh derby of the United Rugby Championship campaign, edging past the Scarlets in Llanelli. Tries from Dan Thomas, Taine Basham, and Evan Lloyd, all stemming from effective attacking line-outs, proved the difference in a 21-15 result. Despite second-half pressure from the hosts, including a penalty from Joe Hawkins, the visitors held firm. The match saw Scarlets vice-captain Ryan Elias mark his 200th appearance for the region, while Cardiff integrated new signings Scott Sio and Le Roux Malan.

teams.heading: Les Kiss prioritises aerial strength for massive Test against South Africa
teams.body: Coach Les Kiss has reshaped his backline to counter the Springboks’ tactical kicking game, handing Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii a starting role on the wing for Sunday’s clash in Perth. Kiss described the encounter as a "massive, massive Test" against a formidable opponent that is several players deep in every position. The coach hopes his selection, combined with a bench packed with forwards, will provide a balanced formula to contain the world champions in what serves as a key World Cup countdown fixture.

teams.heading: Black Ferns women suffer late heartbreak against England at Twickenham stadium
teams.body: The Black Ferns women were denied a historic result in London as Zoe Harrison’s interception try in the final minute secured a 26-19 win for England. Despite leading at half-time following scores from Amy Du Plessis and Ayesha Leti-I’iga, New Zealand found themselves under immense pressure in the second 40. Mererangi Paul had pulled the side level at 19-19 with 10 minutes remaining, but the late lapse saw the hosts extend their unbeaten run to 41 matches.

teams.heading: Springboks prepare for Les Kiss’s aggressive new-look Wallabies in Perth
teams.body: The Springboks face a pivotal test in Perth as they look to maintain momentum in their final outing before the November European tour. Wallabies coach Les Kiss has shaken up his side, moving Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to the wing to address aerial threats. Rassie Erasmus has responded with 13 changes to his starting XV, tasking players like Marco van Staden and Elrigh Louw with proving their value. Erasmus noted, “You only scrum at number eight,” as he finalises his tactical blueprint for the breakdown battle.
